name: New Delhi Bus Transit Dataset
description: Public transport is one of the major forms of transportation in the world. This makes it vital to ensure that public transport is efficient. This research presents a novel real-time GPS bus transit data for over 500 routes of buses operating in New Delhi. The data can be used for modeling various timetable optimization tasks as well as in other domains such as traffic management, travel time estimation, etc. The paper also presents an approach to reduce the waiting time of Delhi buses by analyzing the traffic behavior and proposing a timetable. This algorithm serves as a benchmark for the dataset. The algorithm uses a constrained clustering algorithm for classification of trips. It further analyses the data statistically to provide a timetable which is efficient in learning the inter- and intra-month variations.
evaluation_method: Regression metrics (MAE, RMSE) for travel-time prediction; clustering metrics (e.g., silhouette) and schedule-adherence / waiting-time reduction for timetable optimization
general_score_metric: MAE / RMSE for predictive tasks; schedule-adherence or average waiting-time reduction for optimization tasks
reputation: Research dataset of niche interest in urban mobility and transit planning with limited mainstream adoption.
notes: Real-world GPS traces with missing/noisy readings and temporal coverage variability; moderate scale (hundreds of routes). Multiple downstream tasks are possible but there is no single standardized leaderboard; non-LLM dataset.
